description:
Check whether figures a report STATES can be reproduced by the engine from the SEC facts the report cites. For each `{ token, ticker, fact_ids }` it tries every registered margin, growth, share-of, difference and ratio formula over those facts and compares the rendered result to your token EXACTLY. Use it for a figure that has no `fact_id` or `derived_id` of its own (the model worked it out, or retyped it) — never to invent a figure.

Per item: `cited` (your token is an exact quote of one cited fact's display: cite that `fact_id`), `derived` (exactly one formula reproduces it: cite the returned `derived_id` like a fact_id), `reformatted` (your token is a rounding of a cited fact such as "$403B" for "$402.83B": quote the returned `display` instead), `ambiguous` (two or more different formulas reproduce it: a person must choose, never auto-pass), `none` (nothing reproduces it: treat as unsupported) or `error` (the cited facts could not be read).

Up to 50 items per call, each with 1–20 cited `fact_ids` (64-char hex, from a tool result) of ONE company; at most 5 distinct companies per call (chunk larger sets). Every fact is read from your own plan's data; `as_of_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) drops facts accepted after it. Read-only; available on all plans.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cut (YYYY-MM-DD): a cited fact accepted after this date is not used.

items.description: The figures to check, 1–50; one call per report, not one per figure.

fact_ids.description: The facts cited near the figure (1–20), exactly as tool results gave them.

ticker.description: Ticker or CIK of the company the cited facts belong to.

token.description: The figure exactly as written in the prose, e.g. "46.21%" or "$403B".

name: match_derived

_meta.description: Provenance envelope — data lineage for every MCP response

cost_usd.description: Per-call cost transparency. Omitted for subscription-only tools that have no PAYG-equivalent price.

basis.description: payg_charge = real pay-per-call charge (a card or MPP payment through agent-pay). payg_rate_card = indicative price, not billed.

billed.description: true = this amount was actually charged via PAYG for this call. false = indicative PAYG-equivalent value only: no charge was made for this call (it was within your plan).

data_plan.description: Access plan: sample | sp500 | pro | full

data_quality.description: Server-side invariants run on this response

fundamentals_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the FINANCIAL STATEMENTS were last rebuilt in bulk. Use THIS — not `last_updated` — when telling a user how current the cross-sectional fundamentals are. The snapshot is republished on every weekday price refresh while the statements are carried forward unchanged, so `last_updated` can be far more recent than the numbers it sits next to. It is a floor for a single filer, not a ceiling: a filer with a live partition receives its filing, facts and ratios intraday (minutes after EDGAR dissemination), so an entity-scoped read may carry a filing newer than this; cross-sectional ranks (factor scores, earnings signals) refresh with the weekly bulk export.

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp when the snapshot was exported

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this tool call took, measured server-side around the handler.

limit_warnings.description: Soft-warning array for partial fulfillment. Each entry carries a stable subcode + remediation.options[]. AI agents pattern-match on subcode.

payg_override.description: Set when this single response was paid for via the agent-pay PAYG flow — the rate-limit / depth-limit checks were bypassed for this call only.

pit_safe.description: true iff a zero-look-ahead point-in-time cut was applied to every returned figure

price_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the price surfaces were last refreshed.

reset_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the window resets

truncation.description: Set when fewer rows were returned than requested — explains why and points to a remedy

results.description: One entry per item, in the order sent.

candidates.description: outcome ambiguous: the competing candidates (at most 6). Never auto-pass; a person chooses.

derived_id.description: A citable id: a `drv1:` derived_id, or a fact_id for a rounding of a cited fact.

cited_display.description: outcome reformatted from a cited fact: that fact's exact display.

cited_fact_id.description: outcome reformatted from a cited fact: that fact's id.

derived.description: outcome derived / derived reformatted: formula and input facts behind `derived_id`.

inputs.description: The cited facts the figure is recomputed from (`fact_id` is a literal key).

derived_id.description: outcome derived (or a derived reformatted): the citation id to use, like a fact_id.

display.description: The exact rendering to quote (derived, reformatted).

error.description: outcome error: ENTITLEMENT_DENIED, INPUT_NOT_FOUND (no cited fact readable at as_of_date) or a transient code.

fact_id.description: outcome cited: the cited fact whose display the token quotes exactly.

outcome.description: cited = the token is an exact quote of exactly one cited fact's display; derived = exactly one candidate reproduces the token; reformatted = the token is a rounding of a cited fact or derived figure, quote `display` instead; ambiguous = two or more different candidates reproduce it; none = nothing reproduces it; error = the cited facts could not be read.

rounded.description: outcome derived: true when the token is a rounding (2+ significant digits) of `display`, the engine's unrounded figure.

ticker.description: The uppercased ticker (or CIK) the item asked about.

token.description: The figure exactly as you sent it.

title: Match Derived Figures
